title: Time Fantasy- Not enough slots for content

posts.author: JasonHebert1
posts.body:
Hey all,
So, I recently took the plunge and bought RPG Maker MV along with the Time Fantasy Bundle Pack that comes with about 12 or so of the Time Fantasy content packs.
I've figured out, at least I believe, how to install it, but I'm running into certain issues.
First, how I'm installing is simply adding them into the Resource Manager and then going into the Database and creating maps to slide them into the A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, B, C, D, and E slots.
This is where my problems begin.  My first issue was on the TIme Fantasy "Outside" map when it had 2 variations for A5 (labelled A51 and A52)-  They're duplicates of each other with one being sand and the other being cement.  I hope it's not just "You have to choose 1"?  I'd like to mix them and make use of everything I bought.
And even if it was for that scenario, as I go through I've found much worse cases.  One pack has 4 or 5 for B, another has multiple for C, etc.  Since I can't assign multiple sheets into each slot and can only do 1, how on earth do I make use of all this content?
And to make sure I'm clear, this is NOT just an "abundance of options" content, because each piece is not complete.  For example, one B might have the front tiles for houses and the other B has the roof tiles, etc.  So you actually CAN'T just pick one.
Very confused right now and hoping I can rectify this- All this stuff cost almost 200 dollars!!!
Thanks for any help!!!
-Jay

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
I mean, if it all fit onto the given sheets, you'd have less content in total ;D
I think the thought behind it is rather: I'll arrange everything as well as I can and let people choose between alternate sheets with the extra option of putting together their own sheets if they need it.
While I don't make packs, I often struggle with those things, too, especially when there are plenty of possible combinations. Either I set a few up and hope those are the ones people actually want, or I leave it in bits and hope that people do the minor assembly work themselves or I post massive sheets that need to be sliced into the actual sheets. None is perfect in itself and someone will always be unhappy with each.
Maybe before you get yourself too much into the whole thing, some tips:
If the A1-A4 is one version each, and A5 seems to be a choice between two things, maybe just start by choosing different sheets and just build different "sets" in the editor.
Just for example:
A1-A4 are fix, and for your area, you know which A5 you need.
And then, no slicing and dicing, just selecting in the editor, cause the letters B-E can be used interchangebly, those sheets bascially work the same: The B-E's can go into any of those four slots, so you just pick the four of the sheets that you need for that area, or even just that one map. You likely don't need them all at once, right? And then you start mapping and get yourself more into making the game, and if you have the time and need you can still learn to asseble tilesets in Gimp or a similar program.
Start with the maps you can do that way and use that time to get a better understanding of tilesets and mapping

Open in Aseprite, see palette on the left, unlock if needed, swap color, generate new palette, are all in one place. The wording is much more obvious, there is no floating layers when copying/moving, snap to grid is strict, all in all much more intuitive and will speed up your tweaking. And retain the smallest file size… something I find is a hassle in GIMP as saving the PNG with alpha retained would often double or triple the file size.
I didn’t know what I was missing until I had bought it honestly. I only use GIMP for working with pictures and faces. For everything else, Aseprite.
